distinguishing_features: Embeds a piezoresistive nanocomposite (CNT/polymer) within the blanket itself so swelling strain is transduced directly into resistance change
Uses dedicated embedded electrodes rather than inferring failure from existing external flow/pressure telemetry
Provides a calibrated quantitative strain-to-resistance transfer (gauge factor) tied to a swelling threshold, rather than a proxy signal prone to confounding load variations
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Providing continuous in-situ early detection of blanket swelling before registration drift, without disassembly or reliance on indirect external process telemetry.
parsed.viable_reason: A CNT/polymer piezoresistive response of ~2 gauge factor gives a 10% resistance change at 5% swelling, detectable with standard resistance monitoring, so the mechanism is physically plausible and testable as written with the stated protocol.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The closest art detects failure via inference from external telemetry with confounder normalization; embedding a sensing nanocomposite network inside the monitored body to transduce the failure precursor directly is a different mechanism, not a routine parameter change.
